He was convicted of beating to death, by staff and over a private grudge while in Liangzhou, Fanhe Assistant Magistrate Liu Wu; he was liable for death, but was reduced to commoner, exiled to Quanzhou, and died there.
The literal English is ungrammatical ('convicted for in Liangzhou beating').
The emperor composed a poem in his memory and posthumously made him grand general of the left guard and Duke of Xing, with the posthumous name Xiang, and had him buried near Zhaoling.
The emperor composed a poem in his memory and posthumously made him grand general of the left guard and Duke of Cheng, with the posthumous name Xiang, and had him buried near Zhaoling.
郕國公 is the Duke of Cheng (郕), not Xing (邢).
The emperor composed a poem to mourn him, posthumously appointing him Grand General of the Left Guard and Duke of the State of Xing, with posthumous title Xiang, and burial attendant at Zhaoling.
The emperor composed a poem to mourn him, posthumously appointing him Grand General of the Left Guard and Duke of the State of Cheng, with posthumous title Xiang, and burial attendant at Zhaoling.
郕國公 is the state of Cheng, not Xing.
Thereupon with Hou Junji he advanced and pacified Gaochang; in battle he had merit, and an imperial letter of seal-script comforted and rewarded him.
Thereupon with Hou Junji he advanced and pacified Gaochang; in battle he had merit, and a sealed imperial letter comforted and rewarded him.
璽書 is a sealed imperial letter, not a letter in seal script; 尉勞 is 慰勞, to comfort and reward.

Liang Prefecture is desolate and obstructed—you should find a way to bring quiet there."
涼州荒梗 says Liangzhou itself is desolate and blocked, not the road to it.
I am old and may not live to see the dawn. Grant me but one sight of your accession, and I shall die content."
I am old and fear I may be met by the morning dew first. Grant me but one sight of your accession, and I shall die content."
恐先朝露 is the morning-dew metaphor for dying first, not failing to see the dawn.

Critics complained that Jiao had been favored too lavishly. Because he was an old companion from the prince's household, the emperor wished to make his merits plain and issued an edict: "Director of the palace directorate and Duke of Chu Jiao served me in my princely days. Even Pengzu sharing the same texts, or Ziling as a fellow student, would not have surpassed it.
不過也 means those famous bonds would not have exceeded this one; the English reverses the comparison.

不過也 means the famous pairs would not have surpassed this companionship.

An edict spared him from death, had him beaten, and exiled him to Qinzhou.
欽州 is Qinzhou, not the Qin (秦) prefecture the shortened English suggests.
An edict spared him from execution by special grace, had him beaten with the staff, and exiled him to Qin Prefecture.
An edict spared him from the death penalty, had him beaten with the staff, and exiled him to Qinzhou.
免殊死 means spared from capital punishment, not spared by special grace; 欽州 is Qinzhou.
His younger brother Hui was again Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and held power and favor; Song Jing considered this not a policy for long peace and requested to reduce and restrain them.
His younger brother Hui was also Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and held power and favor; Song Jing considered this not a policy for long peace and requested to reduce and restrain them.
又為 here is "also served as," matching the idiomatic "also," not a repeated appointment.

Qingchu was born just as his father died. The emperor had promised him an imperial princess, but he sank into banishment for more than twenty years.
淪謫 is falling into banishment or demotion, not mere obscurity.

Qingchu was born just as his father died; the emperor had promised he would marry a princess, but afterward he fell into banishment for more than twenty years.
淪謫 is banishment or demotion, not neglect.

In the tenth year, he was charged with leaking words from within the forbidden precincts; he was impeached by the heir to the Prince of Pu Qiao, and an edict ordered the Secretariat and Chancellery to investigate the facts.
坐 here introduces the charge; the sentence is the impeachment and investigation, not yet the verdict.

In the second year of Wude full mourning was finally allowed, yet many were still pressed back to duty by political necessity, among them Fang Xuanling and Chu Suiliang.
武德二年 is the second year of Wude. The packet has no mapping that supports the Western year 619.

周棘扈籓 is "bristling with thorns and guarding the fences," not a man named Zhou Ji.

The clerks of the bureau often sought patronage to commit wrongdoing; previous heads of selection bristled thorns and guarded the fences, stopping up inside and out, yet still could not prohibit it.
周棘扈籓 is a description of precautions, not the name Zhou Ji.

The emperor heard and consoled him, saying, "At the end of Northern Qi, corrupt officials slandered Hulu Mingyue while Emperor Gao Wei failed to see through it—and the loyal man's house was destroyed.

The emperor heard and encouraged him, saying, "In the past at the end of Qi, corrupt clerks sang songs against Hulu Mingyue; Gao Wei was dim and did not perceive it, until his family was destroyed.
斛律明月 is one man. 其家 is his family, not their families, and 明月 is not "and the Moon."
I may lack their virtue, but at least I am not blind to such slander."
I may lack virtue, but at least I am not blind to such slander."
朕雖不德 is "though I lack virtue," not "their virtue."

The princes will likely be trampled by the empress—I see calamity approaching soon."

The princes will likely be trampled by the empress—I see trouble arising before long."
後 here is the empress, not "what follows."

The imperial stables were thereby gradually replenished.
閑廄 is the imperial stable establishment, not spare stables.
